patients.summary: Retired teacher with hypertension, seropositive RA on methotrexate and prednisone, later hypothyroidism, trigeminal neuralgia, Ramsay Hunt syndrome, type 2 diabetes, stage IIIC high-grade serous ovarian cancer in durable remission, chemotherapy neuropathy and a coiled ruptured AComm aneurysm. Last seen July 2025; AA amyloidosis then takes her to dialysis in May 2026, known to the practice only through outside records.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer her primary care here. Retired teacher, lives in town, has a rheumatologist she likes and plans to keep. Membership explained, she is signing up online tonight. New patient visit offered 9/14 at 9:00, accepted. Records release emailed for her previous primary care office.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 38 pages received from her previous primary care office and filed. Highlights for the new patient visit: hypertension for many years on lisinopril 10 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg. Rheumatoid arthritis managed by outside rheumatology, methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 5 mg daily since early this year. Cholesterol noted as high, managed with diet. Screening mammogram 10/2014 negative (BI-RADS 1). Pap 2013 negative. No allergies listed. Smoked until 2013.

conditions.label: Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

medications.sig: Take 6 tablets (15 mg) by mouth once weekly

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
51 yo woman joining the practice. Taught second and third grade for most of her career, retired, spends most of her free time in the garden.

PMH
- HTN since roughly 2000. Lisinopril 10 + HCTZ 12.5 for years, no side effects. Does not check at home.
- Seropositive RA, also about 15 years. Sees an outside rheumatology group once or twice a year. On MTX 15 mg weekly and pred 5 mg daily since early 2015; hands are much better than last year. They draw her labs some of the time; happy for us to do the q3 month MTX bloods here and send copies.
- High cholesterol per old records, told to watch diet. Not on a statin.
PSH: none.
Meds: as above.
Allergies: none known.
FH: mother had high BP and a brain bleed (subarachnoid) at 68. Father type 2 DM and high cholesterol. A maternal aunt had breast cancer before menopause. Paternal grandmother had RA.
SH: ex-smoker, about 20 pack-years, stopped 2013. Wine once or twice a week. Lives alone.
Gyn: still having periods, irregular lately.

ROS otherwise negative today.

Exam: well appearing. BP 138/86. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Hands: no active synovitis, mild MCP prominence bilaterally. No edema. Skin normal.

A/P
1. HTN: near goal on current two drugs. Recheck next visit, consider home cuff.
2. RA on MTX/prednisone: CBC and CMP today, then every 3 months. Copy to rheum.
3. Hyperlipidemia: fasting lipids at next draw.
4. Long-term steroid: bone density at some point, discussed.
5. Health maintenance: mammogram due 10/2015, will order. Pap 2013 normal. Colonoscopy never done, referral at physical. Flu shot next month at nurse visit.
Return 2 months.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Quadrivalent flu 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Screening questions negative. On methotrexate and prednisone, inactivated vaccine fine. Tolerated well.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Came in early because she is worried about her memory. Since about late spring she keeps losing words mid-sentence and forgets why she walked into a room. Tired by mid-afternoon. Always cold, wears a sweater in the house when others are comfortable. Skin dry, bowels slower. Up about 10 lb without changing anything. Periods heavier and longer the last few months. No headache, no weakness, no mood change she can name. Sleeping ok.

O: Weight up from September. Looks tired but bright, conversation normal. Skin dry. No goiter palpable. Heart slow-normal and regular. Reflexes hard to elicit at the ankles. No edema.

A/P: Picture sounds thyroid until proven otherwise. TSH and free T4 today, plus fasting-ish lipids (ate a light breakfast) and her methotrexate bloods since she is due. If thyroid is off she would like to see an endocrinologist given the memory piece and the steroid; reasonable. Heavy periods, likely part of the same picture, revisit once thyroid addressed.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her. TSH 14, free T4 0.5: overt hypothyroidism, which fits everything she described. Cholesterol 245, LDL 160, likely pushed up by the thyroid. She would prefer endocrinology start the treatment. Referral sent marked soon; endocrine scheduler has a slot 12/7. Methotrexate labs fine.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily, 30 minutes before breakfast

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation (visit 12/07/2015)
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology group
Date of visit: 12/07/2015

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Duffy, 52, for abnormal thyroid tests.

She describes half a year of worsening recall and concentration, fatigue, about ten pounds of unintended weight gain, constant chilliness even in a warm house, drier skin, constipation, and heavier menses. RA on methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg; hypertension on lisinopril and HCTZ. No prior thyroid history, no neck radiation, no biotin, no iodine supplements. No known drug allergies. Mother had hypertension and a subarachnoid hemorrhage at 68; father diabetic with hyperlipidemia.

Exam: pulse 58. Skin dry and cool. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules. Delayed relaxation of the ankle reflexes.

Data from your office 11/09: TSH 14 mIU/L, free T4 0.5 ng/dL, total cholesterol 245, LDL 160.

Impression: overt primary hypothyroidism, almost certainly autoimmune in a woman with RA.

Plan: levothyroxine 75 mcg each morning on an empty stomach, 30 minutes before food and apart from calcium or iron. Recheck TSH in 12 weeks; your office may draw it. Lipids should improve as she becomes euthyroid; reassess then. Memory complaints should be revisited once she is replaced. Happy to see her again as needed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks into levothyroxine 75. Already a bit warmer and less foggy, she thinks. Taking it correctly, before coffee.

BP 146/90 today, repeat similar. She saw a notice in the newspaper about a study of a new blood pressure pill being run by a cardiology group and wants to know if she would qualify. Explained in general terms: randomized, may get placebo, close monitoring. She would like to at least hear the details, so referral sent to their research clinic.

Lipids: LDL 160 in November. Even allowing for the thyroid, with hypertension, ex-smoker and family history, statin is reasonable. Agrees to atorvastatin 40 nightly. Muscle aches reviewed.

Plan: TSH in mid-March. Home BP readings. Next visit June, MTX labs between.

documents.title: MTX labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Counts, liver tests and kidney function normal. Copy faxed to rheumatology.

documents.title: Cardiology research clinic (visit 02/29/2016)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, clinical research office
Date of visit: 02/29/2016

Ms. Duffy met with our research team to learn about a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of an investigational oral antihypertensive. We reviewed the consent document at length, including random assignment to study drug or placebo added to her current regimen, the visit schedule and the blood work required.

History reviewed: long-standing hypertension on lisinopril 10 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg; hyperlipidemia, recently on atorvastatin 40 mg; rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisone; hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg. No known drug allergies. Former smoker.

Seated BP 136/84, pulse 66. Heart and lung exam unremarkable.

After thinking it over she decided not to enroll at this time; the visit frequency and the chance of receiving placebo were her reasons. No study drug was dispensed. We recommend she continue her current antihypertensives under your care.

documents.title: Your March results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Renee, thyroid level is now normal at 3.4 on the 75 mcg dose, so no change. LDL came down to 118 on the atorvastatin. Keep going with both.

documents.title: RE: Your March results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wonderful. I can feel the difference, I finished a whole crossword yesterday. Periods are back to normal too. Thank you!

documents.title: Screening colonoscopy (04/21/2016)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside endoscopy center
Procedure date: 04/21/2016
Indication: average-risk screening, first exam.
Prep: good (BBPS 8). Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve photographed. Withdrawal time 9 minutes.
Findings: normal mucosa throughout. No polyps. Small internal hemorrhoids.
Recommendation: repeat screening colonoscopy in 10 years.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feeling like herself again. Lost a few pounds now that she is back out in the garden. Decided against the cardiology study.
Home BPs low 130s/80s. Office 132/82.
No statin aches.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, hands quiet, no edema.
Plan: continue lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, levothyroxine 75. MTX labs today. Physical in September.

reports.text: Specimen adequate, transformation zone present. Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, age 52.
Interval: thyroid replaced, energy and memory back. Colonoscopy in April clean. Periods regular again.
Meds: lisinopril 10, HCTZ 12.5, atorvastatin 40, levothyroxine 75 mcg, MTX 15 weekly, prednisone 5.
No allergies. Ex-smoker since 2013.
ROS negative.
Exam: BP at goal. HEENT normal. Thyroid normal size. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, nipples normal. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, Pap with HPV collected; bimanual without masses or tenderness. Joints without synovitis. Skin without concerning lesions.
PHQ-2 0.
Plan: Pap/HPV, one-time hepatitis C and HIV screening, A1c, TSH, CMP, CBC. Tdap and flu today. Mammogram ordered. Bone density next year given prednisone.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO views with tomosynthesis. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion. Compared with outside study 10/2014.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For a few weeks, jolts of pain in her cheek like an electric shock, a few seconds each, many times a day. Chewing sets them off, as does touching a certain spot when washing her face. Eating less because of it. Fine in between. No fever, no vision trouble, no numbness or weakness. Dentist looked last week and found nothing.
O: Afebrile. Face symmetric. Sensation intact in all three trigeminal divisions. Corneal reflexes present. Teeth and gums unremarkable. Cranial nerves otherwise normal. No lymphadenopathy.
A: Sounds like trigeminal neuralgia.
P: MRI brain to look for a structural cause, neurology referral (first available 12/12). Tylenol in the meantime; she asked to hold off on starting anything until neurology sees her.

reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain. No mass lesion. No demyelinating plaques; no periventricular or callosal white matter lesions. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. No acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No hemorrhage. Trigeminal nerves symmetric in their cisternal course. Paranasal sinuses clear.
reports.conclusion: No mass lesion or demyelinating disease.

medications.sig: Take 1/2 tablet twice daily for 7 days, then 1 tablet twice daily

documents.title: Neurology consultation (visit 12/12/2016)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology practice
Date of visit: 12/12/2016

Reason for referral: paroxysmal facial pain.

Ms. Duffy is a 53-year-old right-handed retired teacher, seen previously by endocrinology for hypothyroidism and by cardiology. For several weeks she has had abrupt stabbing, electrical pain in the cheek, each attack lasting seconds but recurring through the day. Chewing and a light touch over particular spots on the cheek provoke them. Between attacks she is well. She has had no fevers, visual change, limb weakness or numbness.

Other history: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, seropositive RA on methotrexate and prednisone, hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 75 mcg. No drug allergies.

Examination between attacks: alert, fluent. Pupils equal and reactive, fields full, fundi normal. Facial movement symmetric. Corneal reflexes present bilaterally. Facial sensation preserved to light touch and pinprick in V1 to V3. Hearing grossly normal. Tongue and palate midline. Strength, reflexes, coordination and gait normal.

MRI brain from 12/01 reviewed: no mass and no demyelinating lesions.

Assessment: classical trigeminal neuralgia.

Plan: carbamazepine 100 mg twice daily for one week, then 200 mg twice daily. Would check CBC, sodium and liver tests in about four weeks. Warned about dizziness, rash and sleepiness. Follow up with us in three months or sooner if attacks persist.

documents.title: Carbamazepine labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium, liver tests and blood counts all normal on carbamazepine and MTX. Copies to neurology and rheumatology. Pt notified via portal.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up (visit 01/30/2017)
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology group
Date of visit: 01/30/2017

Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, long-standing. Morning stiffness under 15 minutes. No flares since the autumn. Exam: no swollen joints, two mildly tender MCPs, full grip. Labs from your office reviewed and normal.

Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 5 mg daily. Agree with bone density given steroid exposure. Interval note made of carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia. Return in one year.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Age 54, here fasting for her yearly exam.
Interval: trigeminal neuralgia controlled on carbamazepine. Mammogram and bone density in October both normal. RA quiet.
Meds reviewed, unchanged. NKDA.
Periods now infrequent, last about three months ago. No hot flashes to speak of.
ROS: negative.
Exam: well. BP ok. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts normal. Abdomen soft. Joints without synovitis. Skin ok. Face symmetric.
PHQ-2 1.
Plan: fasting labs including A1c (father diabetic, on prednisone), lipids, TSH, MTX bloods. Flu done in October. Pap next 2021. Colonoscopy 2026. Return 3 months.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Renee, a few things to go over. Your fasting sugar was 162 and the A1c 7.8%, which is in the diabetes range. LDL 145, higher than last year. Thyroid and the methotrexate labs are fine. I'd like to repeat the A1c and talk it through in person in about 6 weeks; the front desk will call. No need to worry, but please cut back on sweets in the meantime.

documents.title: RE: Results from your physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Oh dear. Dad had it so I suppose I am not surprised. I'll make the appointment.

documents.title: Triage call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt woke yesterday with severe right ear pain; this morning the right side of her mouth droops and she can't fully close the right eye. Food tastes off. No headache, no arm or leg weakness, speech clear. Same-day appointment 11:30 with PCP; told to call 911 for any weakness or slurred speech.

events.reason: right ear pain and facial weakness

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Same-day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Right ear pain since yesterday, sharp and constant, worse turning her head. Since this morning right face drooping and taste dulled. No vertigo. No limb symptoms. On MTX and pred.
O: Afebrile. Right ear canal with a cluster of small vesicles on a red base; drum looks normal. Right facial weakness involving the forehead, incomplete eye closure. Rest of neuro exam normal: speech, limbs, gait.
A: Peripheral right facial palsy with ear vesicles, most consistent with herpes zoster oticus in an immunosuppressed patient.
P: Spoke with ENT on call, who will see her first thing tomorrow and start treatment there. Eye care: lubricating drops by day, ointment and taping at night. She will hold today's planned errands and go home to rest.

conditions.label: Herpes zoster oticus (Ramsay Hunt syndrome), right

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily for 7 days
Take 3 tablets (60 mg) daily for 5 days, then taper per ENT schedule back to usual 5 mg

documents.title: Otolaryngology consultation (visit 12/05/2017)
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology practice
Date of visit: 12/05/2017

Ms. Duffy is a 54-year-old woman on methotrexate and prednisone for RA, with a history of trigeminal neuralgia, seen urgently at your request.

HPI: right otalgia from 12/03, unrelenting and sharp, aggravated by head movement; reduced taste since yesterday; right facial weakness first noticed yesterday morning.

PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, RA, hypothyroidism, trigeminal neuralgia. Your office's labs of 11/27 noted: fasting glucose 162, A1c 7.8%, total cholesterol 210, HDL 45, LDL 145.
Meds: lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, levothyroxine 75 mcg, methotrexate, prednisone 5 mg, carbamazepine. NKDA.

Vitals within normal limits; BP 130/85.
Exam: erythematous vesicular eruption within the right external auditory canal. Tympanic membrane intact and mobile, no middle ear effusion, no evidence of acute otitis media. Partial right facial paralysis including the brow. Left face normal. No nystagmus. Weber midline.

Impression: herpes zoster oticus (Ramsay Hunt syndrome), right, with incomplete facial nerve paralysis.

Plan: valacyclovir 1 g three times daily for seven days. Prednisone 60 mg daily for five days then taper back to her baseline 5 mg; her glucose will run high on this and should be watched given the A1c. Eye protection reinforced. Electroneurography arranged for 12/11; if degeneration exceeds 90%, we would discuss surgical decompression.

procedures.procedure: Facial nerve decompression, right, middle cranial fossa approach

documents.title: Right facial nerve decompression (12/13/2017)
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside hospital, otology service
Date of surgery: 12/13/2017

Preoperative diagnosis: right herpes zoster oticus with facial paralysis; electroneurography 12/11 showing greater than 90% degeneration on the right.
Procedure: right facial nerve decompression, middle cranial fossa approach (labyrinthine segment, geniculate ganglion and meatal foramen), with transmastoid decompression of the tympanic and mastoid segments.
Anesthesia: general. Stress-dose steroids given.
Findings: edematous nerve at the meatal foramen and geniculate ganglion; sheath opened. No CSF leak.
EBL minimal. No complications.

Discharge summary: discharged 12/15 after uneventful recovery. Wounds clean. Hearing grossly preserved. Glucose 190s to 230s on the steroid course, managed with sliding scale insulin while inpatient; please follow. Resume home medications; finish prednisone taper to 5 mg. ENT clinic follow-up in two weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks out from right facial nerve decompression for Ramsay Hunt. Finished valacyclovir. Prednisone taper ends this weekend, back to 5 mg. Ear pain much less. Thinks she can wrinkle the right brow a little now.
Hospital sent her home with a glucometer; fasting readings 180 to 230 on the high-dose steroid, coming down this week.
Exam: incision behind and above the right ear healing, no redness. Right face weak but some movement of brow and mouth, eye closes with effort. Cornea clear.
A/P: Ramsay Hunt, recovering after decompression; ENT following. Hyperglycemia on top of an A1c of 7.8: keep checking fasting sugars once a day, repeat A1c in mid-January as planned once the steroid burst is behind her.
